description: MassFlow FISH intrinsic families — mine blocks, markers, extracted markers, drawpoints, draw periods, and model-level state. FISH is the only scripted access to any of them: the massflow binary exposes no MassFlow-specific Python module.

usage_pattern.iteration: loop foreach local mb massflow.mineblock.list ... end_loop
usage_pattern.assignment: an intrinsic whose signature ends in ':= <type>' can be written, e.g. massflow.mineblock.frag.primary.a(mb) = 1.0

live_verification: 175 massflow.* intrinsics captured from `fish list intrinsics` on live MassFlow 9.7.47; 81 of them have no page in the 9.7 manual and are marked `documented: false`. State-grade spot checks on the tutorial model: massflow.mass.total, massflow.day, massflow.period, massflow.mineblock.fric, massflow.marker.type, massflow.extractedmarker.num, massflow.drawperiod.num (59 imported periods) and massflow.period.days(1) (7-day period) all returned values consistent with the model that produced them. The per-period massflow.drawperiod.* accessors did not, and their family file says so.

retired.name: massflow.mass.extracted
retired.note: Has a page in the 9.7 manual but is gone from the binary: evaluating it answers 'massflow.mass.extracted is not recognized as a library function'. Use massflow.mass.total.

retired.name: massflow.mineblock.friction
retired.note: Has a page in the 9.7 manual but is gone from the binary: evaluating it answers 'massflow.mineblock.friction is not recognized as a library function'. Use massflow.mineblock.fric.

official_documentation: Itasca 9.7 MassFlow manual, FISH Functions (96 fish_massflow.* pages)
